survey: A blue cartoon anchor floating on a striped orange background, with no ground. The anchor lies nearly flat to the camera and is rotated slightly clockwise, so the shank leans right as it rises. The round ring sits on top of the shank and reads as a near-circle, which fits a ring whose plane faces the viewer. The crossbar (stock) goes through a cylindrical collar near the top. It stays roughly at right angles to the shank and dips slightly to the right, matching the shank's lean. Its two ball ends are the same size, which fits a flat view. At the bottom, the curved arms and the pointed crown share the same slight rotation. Both arm tips sit on a line roughly at right angles to the shank, and their bevels are lit and foreshortened alike. A tan rope loops through the ring and winds down around the shank. It passes behind and in front of the shank in a believable spiral, and it narrows evenly where it wraps the round shank. Every part agrees on one nearly face-on view with a mild rotation in the picture plane. The only design liberty is that the stock lies in the same plane as the arms, where a real anchor's stock sits at right angles to them. That is a choice about the object, not a perspective mistake.
